comparator.name: Biotechnology (Bachelor Biotechnologie)
comparator.academicYear: Current WUR programme and cohort-2025 curriculum, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The official programme is a three-year, 180-EC bachelor combining biology, chemistry, mathematics and process engineering. Years 1 and 2 each account for 60 EC in cell biology, microbiology, biochemistry, chemistry, mathematics, cell-factory and bioreactor design, process engineering, genetics, statistics, protein biochemistry, gene technology and separation-process design. The programme describes Biology and Engineering directions; Biology is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break because it is listed first, while published restricted choices remain generic. Year 3 contains a 24-EC laboratory thesis, 6 EC restricted choice and 30 EC genuine free choice/minor space.

components.name: Year 1 biotechnology foundation
components.note: Complete published year comprising Organic Chemistry 1 and 2, Thermodynamics, Applied Mathematics: Analysis and Linear Algebra, Mathematics for Biotechnologists, General Chemistry 1 and 2, Bioprocess Engineering Basics, Basic Cell Factory Design, Introduction Biotechnology 1, Cell Biology, Microbiology and Biochemistry, and Practical Biological Chemistry.

components.name: Year 2 biological and engineering development
components.note: Complete published year comprising Analytical Methods in Organic Chemistry, Bioreactor Design, Statistics, Cell Physiology and Genetics, Biotechnology 2, Protein Biochemistry, Microbial Physiology Technology, a restricted option, Communication and Gene Technology, and Separation Process Design.

components.name: Restricted option
components.note: Published restricted choice; no particular module is invented.

components.name: Open elective or minor space
components.note: Genuine free-choice space; no package is invented.

notes.text: WUR Biotechnology contains dedicated organic and analytical chemistry, thermodynamics, cell-factory and bioreactor design, separation-process engineering and a 24-EC laboratory thesis. UCR can construct strong molecular, medical and modelling pathways but lacks a continuous bioprocess-engineering sequence. The alternatives are defensible related biotechnology programmes, not engineering-degree equivalence.
